items: Identify Your Contract Type: Open a document and write down whether your most common work is deliverable-based, hourly, or retainer so you choose the correct template for each engagement.

Select the Right Contract Archetype: Match your contract structure to your work type—use deliverable-based for defined outputs, hourly for uncertain scope, and retainer for ongoing relationships where you need predictable income.

Document Your Contract Template: Before your next client engagement, download or draft a contract template for whichever archetype fits your work so you never start a project without a signed agreement.
Match Contract Type to Work Style: Review each of your current projects and assign the appropriate contract archetype to each one, ensuring you have the right structure for every engagement.

Define Revision Limits in Writing: Specify exactly how many revision rounds are included, what counts as a revision versus a redesign, and the rate you'll charge for additional rounds so clients can't demand free work.

Lock In Your Payment Schedule: State deposit amounts, progress payment triggers, and final payment requirements as percentages tied to specific project milestones so you always know when money is due.
Add a Kill Fee Clause: Include a clause specifying what percentage of remaining contract value you receive if a client cancels mid-project so you don't work for free on aborted projects.
Protect Your Intellectual Property: Add a clause stating that IP transfers to the client only upon final payment so you retain leverage when clients delay paying their final invoice.

Create a Scope Change Request Form: Draft a simple form clients must use to formally request changes, including a description field and estimated impact on timeline and budget so every request is documented.

Require Written Approval Before Changes: Specify in your contract that no additional work begins until you provide a written estimate and the client approves it in writing so you never do unpaid work.
Quote Your Change Fees Upfront: When a client requests a change, calculate the additional cost and send it to them before doing any work so there's no dispute about payment later.

Add Milestone Check-Ins to Every Project: Schedule regular check-ins throughout your project where you review progress against the original scope and flag any drift immediately so scope creep doesn't accumulate unnoticed.
